chapter.title: Social Science: Contemporary India - II (NCERT Class 10 Geography)

terminology.definition: Everything available in our environment which can be used to satisfy our needs, provided it is technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally acceptable.

definitions.definition: Development that satisfies present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs or damaging the environment.
definitions.source_context: Rio Earth Summit 1992 / Brundtland Commission Report

definitions.definition: Total physical area sown with crops and harvested within an agricultural year.
Total area sown once or more than once in an agricultural year (Net Sown Area + area sown multiple times).
Cropland left uncultivated for one or less than one agricultural year to naturally restore soil nutrients.
Farmland left uncultivated for more than 5 consecutive agricultural years.
Institutional program involving local village communities to manage and restore degraded state forests in exchange for non-timber produce.
Floor price announced by the government prior to sowing seasons to guarantee farmers against distress selling.

concepts.title: Interdependent Triangle of Resource Creation
concepts.explanation: Human beings interact with nature through technology and build institutions to transform materials into resources.

concepts.title: Stock vs Reserves
concepts.explanation: Stock refers to environmental materials with potential to meet human needs but lacking technological access. Reserves are a subset of stock that can be utilized with existing technology but are stored for future use.

concepts.title: Quantitative vs Qualitative Water Scarcity
concepts.explanation: Quantitative scarcity is a physical deficit in water volume relative to population. Qualitative scarcity occurs when abundant water is contaminated by industrial, agricultural, and urban pollution.

concepts.title: Three-Stage Effluent Treatment
concepts.explanation: Primary (mechanical screening & sedimentation), Secondary (biological treatment & aeration), Tertiary (chemical recycling to achieve zero liquid discharge).

facts.fact: India's total geographical land area is 3.28 million square kilometers, with land utilization data available for 93%.
India possesses approximately 8% of the total global species richness, estimating nearly 1.6 million species.
Reserved and Protected forests together account for two-thirds of India's total forest area.
Fresh water constitutes only 2.5% of total global water resources, with the majority trapped in ice sheets and glaciers.
Magnetite is the finest quality iron ore containing up to 70% iron with excellent magnetic properties.
India's road network spans approximately 5.6 million kilometers, forming one of the largest road systems in the world.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.contribution: Voiced deep concern over resource conservation: 'There is enough for everybody's need and not for any body's greed.'

people.name: Vinoba Bhave
people.contribution: Initiated the Bhoodan-Gramdan movement ('Bloodless Revolution') at Pochampally for voluntary land redistribution.

people.name: Shri Ram Chandra Reddy
people.contribution: Offered 80 acres of land to 80 landless villagers in Pochampally, sparking the Bhoodan movement.

people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
people.contribution: Proclaimed multi-purpose dams as the 'Temples of Modern India' to integrate agricultural development with industrialization.

chronology.milestone: 1854: First modern textile mill established in Mumbai.
1947: Post-independence development of Kandla port in Gujarat.
1952: Asiatic Cheetah declared officially extinct in India.
1972: Enactment of the Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act.
1973: Launch of Project Tiger across Indian national reserves.
1988: Odisha passes first resolution for Joint Forest Management.
1992: United Nations Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro adopts Agenda 21.

cause_effect.cause: Tube-well over-irrigation in Punjab and Haryana
cause_effect.effect: Waterlogging leads to increased soil alkalinity and salinity, causing land degradation.

cause_effect.cause: Open-cast mining in Jharkhand and Odisha
cause_effect.effect: Severe forest destruction and abandoned mine pits left with overburden waste.
Heavy sedimentation makes stream beds rockier, disrupts fish spawning, and exacerbates seasonal flooding.

cause_effect.cause: High sucrose content and cooler coastal climate in Maharashtra
cause_effect.effect: Shift of sugarcane cultivation and cooperative mills from UP to Maharashtra.

geographical_features.description: Formed by volcanic lava flows; covered with moisture-retentive Black (Regur) soil ideal for cotton.
Rich in high-grade iron ore, coking coal, bauxite, and mica; hub of India's heavy metallurgical steel plants.
Provides abundant fresh water, cheap river freight, and raw material access for India's jute mill cluster.

historical_concepts.explanation: Colonial forestry replaced diverse natural mixed forests with single commercial species (e.g., teak, pine), causing long-term ecological degradation.
Century-old indigenous hydrological engineering such as Guls/Kuls in Himalayas, Khadins in Jaisalmer, and Johads in Alwar.

civic_concepts.explanation: Active participation of local indigenous populations in natural resource decision-making (e.g. Chipko Movement, JFM, Sariska legal resistance).
Traditional cultural belief systems preserving virgin forest patches as sacred realms of deities, prohibiting commercial exploitation.

economic_concepts.concept: Primary vs Secondary vs Tertiary Sectors
economic_concepts.explanation: Primary sector (agriculture, mining) extracts natural resources; Secondary sector (manufacturing) transforms raw materials into finished goods; Tertiary sector (transport, trade, banking) provides support services.

economic_concepts.concept: Favorable vs Unfavorable Balance of Trade
economic_concepts.explanation: Favorable trade balance occurs when export value exceeds import value. Unfavorable occurs when import value exceeds export value.
Foreign tourists spend foreign exchange directly on hospitality, transport, and handicrafts, functioning as a high-value invisible export.
